diagnostics.message: aws_cloudfront_distribution.default builds its S3 origin from local.cf_access.path (which resolves to aws_cloudfront_origin_access_identity.default[0].cloudfront_access_identity_path). Because that value is threaded through the cf_access_options conditional-map workaround, the dependency graph records no edge, and unlike the origin bucket there is no compensating depends_on. The origin access identity must be created before the distribution that references its access-identity path, so add depends_on = [aws_cloudfront_origin_access_identity.default] (nested s3_origin_config block prevents a clean scalar data reference).

With CloudFront access logging enabled (default), aws_cloudfront_distribution.default's logging_config.bucket is local.cf_log_bucket_domain, which resolves to module.logs.bucket_domain_name when cloudfront_access_log_create_bucket is true (default). That reference goes through a local, so the graph shows no dependency, and there is no depends_on. The log bucket must exist (with the awslogsdelivery ACL) before CloudFront logging can be enabled, so the distribution should depend on module.logs (nested logging_config block prevents a clean scalar data reference).
